facts.statement: The genus Laganosuchus was first described by Sereno and Larsson in 2009.
Fossils of Laganosuchus date to the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Cenomanian age.
Laganosuchus is classified as an extinct genus of stomatosuchid crocodyliform.
facts.quote: Laganosuchus is an extinct genus of stomatosuchid crocodyliform.

facts.statement: Fossils of Laganosuchus have been found in Niger and Morocco.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from Niger and Morocco and date back to the Upper Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The name Laganosuchus means "pancake crocodile" because of its shallow skull depth.
facts.quote: The name means "pancake crocodile" from the Greek λαγανον, ("pancake") and σοῦχος, ("crocodile") in reference to the shallow depth of the skull

facts.statement: The discoverers Paul Sereno and Hans Larsson nicknamed the animal "PancakeCroc".
facts.quote: It has been nicknamed "PancakeCroc" by Paul Sereno and Hans Larsson

facts.statement: Fossils of both Laganosuchus species are known only from their lower jaws.
facts.quote: Both species of Laganosuchus are known only from their lower jaws

facts.statement: The total jaw length of L. thaumastos was 838 mm.
facts.quote: L. thaumastos had a total jaw length of 838 mm

facts.statement: Each side of the Laganosuchus mouth bore 24 teeth.
facts.quote: Each side of the mouth bore 24 teeth

facts.statement: All the teeth of Laganosuchus were simple straight spikes.
facts.quote: All the teeth were simple straight spikes

facts.statement: The weak symphysis of Laganosuchus suggests it had a very weak bite.
facts.quote: The symphysis itself is relatively small and weak compared to other crocodyliforms, suggesting a very weak bite

facts.statement: It is debated whether Laganosuchus had gular sacs beneath its throat, as there is no fossil evidence to confirm or deny this.
facts.quote: It is possible that they had gular sacs beneath their throats, just as their relative Stomatosuchus may have done, but there is no fossil evidence either to support or disprove this theory.

facts.statement: L. thaumastos was approximately 6 meters long with a 1-meter flat head and was a fish-eater.
facts.quote: According to Sereno and Larsson, L. thaumastos was an approximately 6 m (20 ft) long, squat fish-eater with a 1 m (3.3 ft) flat head.

facts.statement: The tightly fitting teeth of Laganosuchus would have prevented fish from escaping once trapped.
facts.quote: These teeth would have fitted together tightly so that no fish trapped in the mouth could escape.

facts.statement: Laganosuchus belongs to the family Stomatosuchidae.
Laganosuchus lived between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)
